title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: An agent has made five model calls in one session. On the sixth call, where does the model get what happened in the first five?

options.text: It keeps an internal memory of its own earlier calls
The program resends the earlier messages inside the new call
It looks the earlier steps up in its training data
The tools remember and report the earlier steps back

items.stem: An agent's instructions and the student's question take 1,000 tokens. Each step adds 2,000 tokens to the message list, and the whole list is sent on every call. The model is called 5 times. How many input tokens are sent in total across the 5 calls?
Your assistant must remember each student's preferred booking times from one visit to the next. Which design makes that possible?

options.text: Write a short note to storage and read it in next visit
Use a model with a much larger context window size
Keep every visit's messages inside a single running list
Repeat the preferences inside the standing instructions

items.stem: A returning student says, "I finished laser cutter training last month, so book me a slot." The assistant's saved notes also say "laser cutter: trained". In one sentence, what should the assistant rely on to decide whether to book, and how does it get it?

A 300-page machine manual is far larger than your context window budget for one request. In one or two sentences, what does retrieval do so that the assistant can still answer a question about page 212?
